name: Apple
perishability: Storable. 4–6 months in cold store, 8–10 months in controlled atmosphere (CA).
summary: Grown almost entirely in two Himalayan regions, Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh, and harvested in a single July–November window. What happens after that depends on storage and imports: CA stores carry Indian fruit into spring, and imports from Iran, Turkey, the US and others fill the gap until the next harvest.

key_numbers.label: Imports
key_numbers.note: Iran, Turkey, Afghanistan, USA, Chile, NZ, Italy, Poland

global: India is a mid-sized producer and a net importer. Imported apples dominate city shelves from March to July.

rows.hubs: Shopian, Baramulla (Sopore), Pulwama, Kulgam, Anantnag, Kupwara, Budgam
Shimla (Kotkhai, Jubbal, Rohru, Theog, Narkanda), Kinnaur, Kullu, Mandi, Chamba
Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Ladakh; low-chill apple trials in the plains

belts.name: South Kashmir
belts.note: Shopian is the largest apple-growing district in India.

belts.name: North Kashmir
belts.note: Sopore fruit mandi is one of Asia's largest.

belts.name: Shimla upper belt
belts.note: Royal Delicious heartland; corporate buyers set reference prices here.

belts.name: Kinnaur and Lahaul
belts.note: Late, high-colour fruit; the belt is moving uphill as winters warm.

seasons.name: Himachal harvest
seasons.note: 'Sow' here means bloom. Low hills from July; Royal Delicious mid-Aug to Oct; Kinnaur to Nov.

seasons.name: Kashmir harvest
seasons.note: Early types in Aug; Delicious and Ambri Sep–Nov.

seasons.name: From CA storage
seasons.note: Stored Indian fruit sold through winter and spring.

lean_season: March–July: domestic stock runs out and imports set the price.

climate.v: Needs 1,000–1,500 hours below 7 °C in winter (Delicious types). Warm winters reduce flowering and fruit set.
1,000–1,250 mm, well spread; dry, sunny weather with cool nights before harvest builds colour.
Spring frost at bloom (Mar–Apr) kills flowers.

weather_risks.risk: Spring frost and cold rain at bloom
weather_risks.impact: Poor fruit set; whole-season crop loss in exposed orchards.
Scarred fruit drops to the lowest grades; anti-hail nets are spreading.
Harvest-time road closures strand trucks; fruit rots in transit.
weather_risks.example: 2023 Himachal monsoon disaster; repeated NH-44 closures at Ramban.

weather_risks.impact: Breaks branches still in leaf; damages unharvested fruit.
weather_risks.example: Early snow in Nov 2019 and Oct 2018 caused heavy orchard damage.

weather_risks.impact: Insufficient chilling, weak bloom, more pests.

pests.name: Apple scab
pests.impact: Scabby leaves and fruit; historic epidemics in HP and Kashmir.

pests.name: Premature leaf fall (Marssonina blotch)
pests.impact: Early defoliation; widespread in HP and Kashmir since the 2000s.

pests.name: San Jose scale, woolly apple aphid
European red mite
pests.impact: Leaf bronzing in hot dry spells.

pests.name: Root and collar rot, canker
pests.impact: Tree death in poorly drained orchards.

postharvest.storage: Cold store: −1 to 0 °C, 90–95% RH. CA store: 1–2% O₂ and 1–3% CO₂ at about 0 °C.
postharvest.respiration: Climacteric and a strong ethylene producer: store away from cauliflower, leafy greens and bananas.
postharvest.chilling: Most varieties tolerate 0 °C; some suffer low-temperature breakdown below that.
practices: Graded by size (Extra Large to Extra Small and 'pittoo') and colour.
Himachal moved to selling by weight in 2023 (24 kg cap per box) and to standard 'universal cartons' in 2024, ending the old over-filled boxes.
Kashmir trades in 16–18 kg wooden or cardboard boxes.
1-MCP (SmartFresh) and CA extend storage; CA capacity is concentrated in HP (including Adani Agri Fresh), Kashmir and Delhi-NCR.

steps.what: Picked and graded at the orchard; some orchards are leased to contractors before harvest.
Sopore, Shopian, Parimpora (Srinagar), Narwal (Jammu), Parala and Dhalli (Shimla); corporate buyers publish procurement rates.
Most fruit travels on consignment to Azadpur (Delhi) commission agents who auction it and remit after deducting fees.
Part of the crop enters cold or CA storage for sale Dec–May.
Fruit sellers, modern retail and quick commerce, alongside imported apples.

routes.mode: Truck via NH-44 (Banihal), often delayed by closures
Rail parcel services on the new Jammu–Srinagar line (from 2025)

supply_chain.packaging: Standard cartons (HP), wooden or cardboard boxes (Kashmir); trays for premium grades.
supply_chain.farmer_share: Not estimated in the RBI series; commission agents typically charge a fixed percentage plus freight and labour.

markets.name: Azadpur APMC
markets.role: National price setter; most consignments are sold here.

varieties.name: Ambri, Maharaji, American Trel
varieties.note: Kashmiri heritage varieties; Ambri keeps well.

varieties.name: Spur types (Red Chief, Oregon Spur, Super Chief, Scarlet Spur)
Gala, Fuji, Granny Smith, Jeromine, Red Velox
Anna, HRMN-99
varieties.note: Low-chill types tried in the plains.

trade.exports: Small, mostly to Nepal and Bangladesh.
trade.imports: About 5–6 lakh t a year: Iran (largest by volume), Turkey, Afghanistan, USA (Washington), Chile, New Zealand, Italy, Poland, South Africa. Basic duty 50% (Afghanistan duty-free under SAFTA).

policy.what: Minimum import price of ₹50/kg (CIF) on apples, except from Bhutan.
India withdrew the extra retaliatory duty on US apples; MFN duty applies.
Himachal Pradesh made weight-based sale of apples mandatory (2023) and introduced universal cartons (2024).
J&K Market Intervention Scheme (NAFED) used in crisis years such as 2019.

history.what: Communication shutdown in Kashmir disrupted trade; NAFED bought apples under a special MIS.
Early heavy snowfall damaged orchards still in leaf.
Floods and landslides in Himachal blocked roads at harvest; crop also smaller after a poor bloom.
NH-44 closures stranded trucks; rail parcel services from Kashmir started on the new line.

signals: Bloom and hail reports (Mar–Jun) from HP and J&K horticulture departments.
Corporate procurement rates announced in Himachal each August.
CA and cold-store stock levels from Dec; import arrivals and CIF prices from Feb.
business: Storage is the arbitrage: harvest-time prices (Aug–Oct) are the lowest of the year, and CA-stored Indian fruit competes with imports in spring.
Grading and packing standards (weight-based cartons in HP) make apples one of the easiest fruits to buy remotely by spec.
Imports set the ceiling for half the year; the ₹50/kg minimum import price matters mostly for cheap Iranian fruit.
Premium high-density varieties (Gala, Fuji) from new Indian orchards can substitute imports.

institutes.name: Dr YS Parmar University of Horticulture and Forestry

gi: Kashmir apples are not GI-tagged as a whole; 'Kinnauri apple' and others have been proposed
